finding.claim:
Loofah::Helpers.sanitize (and any HTML4-parsed fragment scrubbed with :strip/:prune/:escape/:whitewash) lets a javascript: URL through href when the scheme is obfuscated with the HTML5-only named entity 	 or 
. The sanitizer decodes only : and the five basic entities, so the protocol check sees 'java&tab;script:' and passes it. The browser decodes the entity to a tab, which the URL parser strips, and the link runs script on click.
finding.source: Attacker-supplied HTML string passed to Loofah::Helpers.sanitize, e.g. x. Input goes through the HTML4 (libxml2) parser, which does not know the HTML5-only entity , so the attribute value stays literal.
finding.sink: Browser navigation of the serialized href attribute emitted by helpers.rb:25 (to_s). The allowlist check that should block it is at scrub.rb:176-185.

trace.note: Loofah.html4_fragment: libxml2 HTML4 parser; 	 not an HTML4 entity so attribute value keeps the literal text 'java	script:...'
'a' is in ALLOWED_ELEMENTS_WITH_LIBXML2 (safelist.rb:1052), so element is kept
'href' is in ATTR_VAL_IS_URI (safelist.rb:582-592), so scrub_uri_attribute runs
CGI.unescapeHTML decodes only amp/lt/gt/quot/apos and numeric refs; '	' is left as-is
control chars stripped (no effect: no literal control char present in the attack string)
URI_PROTOCOL_REGEX (line 17) needs [a-z][a-z0-9+\-.]*: from start; 'java&' fails to match, so the protocol check is skipped and allowed_uri? returns true (line 185)
force_correct_attribute_escaping! runs; href is in BROKEN_ESCAPING_ATTRIBUTES (libxml2_workarounds.rb:20-25) but only space and double-quote are rewritten (scrub.rb:217), '&' is untouched
to_s serializes via libxml2 HTML serializer. ASSUMED (not verified in this repo): libxml2 writes href/action/src values without HTML-escaping '&', so output is 'java	script:...' verbatim

finding.guards_checked:
(1) Element allowlist (safelist.rb ACCEPTABLE_ELEMENTS/ALLOWED_ELEMENTS_WITH_LIBXML2): 'a' allowed, so no block. (2) Attribute allowlist (scrub.rb:60): href allowed. (3) URI scheme check (scrub.rb:170-186): bypassed because the unescape step does not decode 	/
. (4) Control-char stripping (scrub.rb:10,173): does not match the entity form, which is only decoded by the browser. (5) : special case (scrub.rb:174): covers only that one entity. (6) force_correct_attribute_escaping! (scrub.rb:202-221): only space and quote for href. (7) Form removal (helpers.rb:24): removes only direct ./form children, and only form elements. Not a guard for <a>. The HTML5 path (loofah.rb:108, html5 fragment) is NOT affected: Gumbo decodes 	 to a real tab before the sanitizer, and CONTROL_CHARACTERS removes it.
finding.repro: Not executed (no shell in this session). Check: Loofah::Helpers.sanitize('x') should return the href unchanged if the bug is present. Preconditions to confirm: the Nokogiri/libxml2 version in use keeps HTML5-only named entities literal in the HTML4 parser and serializes href '&' unescaped. Compare with Loofah.html5_fragment(...).scrub!(:strip) (expected to strip the href).

finding.claim: data: URI mediatype check can classify a malformed mediatype as text/plain (and allow it) when a browser's MIME parser may read the same string as text/html, e.g. 'text/html/x'. Low impact because top-level data: navigation is blocked by modern browsers and no allowed element renders data: HTML.
finding.source: Attacker-controlled href/src value starting with 'data:' containing a malformed mediatype such as 'data:text/html/x,<payload>'.
finding.sink: Protocol/mediatype allowlist decision at scrub.rb:180-183, which keeps the attribute.

trace.note: DATA_URI_MEDIATYPE (lines 34-40) rejects the '/' in subtype, so the code returns 'text/plain', which is in the allowlist

finding.guards_checked: Protocol allowlist (data is in ACCEPTABLE_PROTOCOLS, safelist.rb:992). Mediatype allowlist (text/plain is allowed). Element allowlist: href on 'a' is the only sink that can navigate. Browsers block top-level navigation to data: URLs, and no allowed element (iframe/object/embed) is in the safelist. This means the impact is low and browser-dependent.
finding.repro: Not executed. Verify how target browsers parse 'data:text/html/x,...' and whether the sanitizer's text/plain fallback (line 274) can ever yield a renderable HTML document in an allowed context.
